caveats: Kaggle ran RAG only (embedding, indexing, retrieval, reranking) and wrote per-item retrieved contexts with ids and scores (retrieved_contexts.jsonl, sha256 recorded in run_meta.json). No LLM ran on Kaggle (user directive, 2026-11-04 00:06 IST). An earlier kernel version that served vLLM models, and a leftover v1 judge kernel, were cancelled before producing results.

Generator antigravity/claude-sonnet-4-6 and judge codex/gpt-6-luna were called through OmniRoute from the Hark sandbox (≤4 concurrent, retries with backoff); fallback for either is gpt-5.6-terra, and every item or metric call that used it is listed. Production uses openai/gpt-oss-120b on Groq; Sonnet stands in for it here, so answer quality is not the production model's. No Groq call was made in this eval, so the Groq-to-OmniRoute fallback never fired.

Generation emulates the agent's policy path (deterministic request guards -> boundary templates; prompts.POLICY in the item's language, literacy medium, text channel; answer + citation guards with one rewrite; policy_abstain fallback). Not emulated: the LLM intent classifier (every item is treated as a policy question), the ungrounded-number guard, streaming and Langfuse. Clarify items therefore show what the policy path does, not the full LangGraph agent.

Retrieval rebuilds the index in the kernel from the same cleaned chunks (EmbeddingGemma-2 in float32 because T4 has no bf16; G1 indexed in bf16 on CPU), so vectors can differ slightly from the qdrant_v3 copy. Each question searches both collections; the union is cut to the top 5 by reranker score (the repo has no router yet).

Golden v2 is release candidate saral_golden_v2.0-rc1, frontier-authored, review_status pending_human. Only the 178 dev items were shipped and run. The 49 held-out items were never uploaded, and the eval script aborts if a held-out id appears.

The judge is an LLM (codex/gpt-6-luna). Judge-human agreement has not been measured; the 30 calibration items in PR #44 exist for that. Hindi and Telugu samples are small (9 hi, 11 te dev items), so per-language numbers are indicative only.
Each judge metric is tried at most twice; failures are recorded as unscored, never as a score.

The judge ran in resumable chunks (the sandbox suspends background work between steps), so judge_info.json 'seconds' covers only the last chunk; every metric was scored exactly once in the final file (636 jobs, 0 errors).
not_covered: The full LangGraph agent: intent classification, explain / improve / what-if answers, ZEN decisions, tool calls and multi-turn memory (Golden B, agent_v1, is not run here).
The production generator (gpt-oss-120b on Groq), voice channel, low/high literacy styles, streaming and latency of the real API.
The 49 held-out RAG items and the 30-item human calibration (no judge-human agreement yet).
Retrieval against the deployed Qdrant/query encoder on InstaBox; the index here was rebuilt on Kaggle.
Citation quality beyond the deterministic checks (the citation and figure GEval rubrics were not run in this baseline), and the deterministic ungrounded-number guard.
PII handling, prompt-injection inside retrieved passages, and other applicants' data beyond the few behaviour items.

limitation_causes.Retrieval misses: Reranked top 5 favours sibling chunks or a neighbouring document: for R2-AMT-02 (minimum amount) the rates-and-fees page was outranked by overview/eligibility pages; for R2-DLR-05 (delete my data) Bajaj's privacy/app T&C outranked the RBI consumer-finance direction. No collection router, and both collections compete for 5 slots. Most misses still answered correctly from a sibling chunk (Faithfulness stayed 1.0).
limitation_causes.Unfaithful or unsupported claims: Over-strong paraphrase of qualified policy text: 'up to 36%' stated as exactly 36% (R2-LHR-05), exceptions dropped in the digital-lending disbursal rule (R2-DLR-01), 'dropline limit' turned into 'outstanding limit' (R2-PRE-05). No figure was invented outright in the 149 judged answers.
limitation_causes.Wrong abstain or refuse: Clarify items: the policy prompt has no instruction to ask a clarifying question, and the intent classifier/clarify logic of the full agent was not exercised, so 10 of 11 vague questions got a direct answer (e.g. R2-CLA-03, R2-CLA-08). Over-abstain: the deterministic request guards fire on benign policy questions: 'my friend and I took the same loan' -> other_applicant (R2-RAT-07) and 'credit guarantee scheme fee' -> guarantee (R2-FEE-08); R2-PUR-01 abstained because no passage states per-purpose limits. All 10 refuse and 8 abstain items were handled acceptably by the judge's rubric.
limitation_causes.Hindi and Telugu failures: No wrong-script answers (20/20 in the right script). The few hi/te failures are the same causes as English: a retrieval miss on the RBI-IOS FAQ (R2-LHI-06), a qualified '36%' stated flatly (R2-LHR-05), and conflict notes not made (R2-LHI-03). Samples are small (9 hi, 11 te).
limitation_causes.Conflict-note handling: The POLICY prompt asks to flag [historical] passages but not to surface disagreeing current sources, so the model gives one figure (e.g. ₹75 lakh in R2-AMT-01) without noting the ₹55 lakh conflict; 10 of 11 answer_note items were scored below 1.0.
limitation_causes.Latency or rate-limit fallbacks: No Groq call is made in this eval (OmniRoute stand-ins), so the Groq-to-OmniRoute fallback never fired. Judge stalls happened when in-flight OmniRoute calls hung after sandbox suspension; the judge was re-run in resumable chunks with a 60 s client timeout, and one metric call fell back to gpt-5.6-terra.
limitation_causes.Internal labels shown to the borrower (a: The policy prompt asks for citations as P1..P5 labels, and the model also writes them (and the word 'passages') into the answer text; the agent's citation pipeline maps labels to sources but nothing strips them from the prose. Mostly 'passages'/'P1'; 4 answers say 'bureau'.
